title: Splitting the inner product at a coordinate
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $F$ be a real-valued family indexed by $F_2^{k+1}$ with values that are functions on $F_2^n$, and choose a coordinate $i\in[k+1]$. Its Gowers inner product equals the average over $y\in(F_2^n)^k$ of the product of two slice expectations. For each bit $b\in\mathbb F_2$, the corresponding slice expectation is the average over $x\in F_2^n$ of the product over $s\in F_2^k$ of $F$ evaluated at the point formed by inserting $b$ into coordinate $i$ of $s$, and at $x+\sum_j s_jy_j$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real-valued family on the indicated cubes
